requirements.note: All 260 tickers listed with bold symbol, grey name, price and a tinted % badge with arrow (green ↗ up, red ↘ down). An extra 'Market pulse' advancing/declining card sits above the list.

Prices change every second, a handful of rows at a time, both at rest and while scrolling; rows update in place without jumps. When sorted by change, rows re-sort live, so a row can move just before you tap it (I starred a neighbour once).

Sort menu (Symbol/Price/Change plus Ascending/Descending) in a pinned section header; search by symbol or name ('cedar' gave 16 hits) with a 'No matching symbols' empty state and a Clear search button.
Star on each row turns orange and filled; the All / My List segment filters correctly; My List has an empty state with an 'Explore All' button; there is also a star in the detail nav bar.
Detail shows big price, change since open, open, volume and a filled line chart ('Price activity', range, sample count) that adds samples live, up to 60.
My List (ARI, ZEXO) and the sort (Change ↓) survived relaunch. The search text is cleared on relaunch.

tells: Custom warm off-white/cream background instead of systemBackground / grouped background
Segmented control is a hand-styled tall (45pt) pill rather than the standard UISegmentedControl metrics
Change shown as a tinted pill badge with arrow glyphs: a web/fintech look rather than plain coloured text
Sort control is a custom blue '⇅ Symbol ↑' text button in the section header; its ⇅ glyph doesn't scale with Dynamic Type while the text does
Row stars and the search field don't grow at the largest text size, while the rest of the row does
At the largest text size the pinned '260 SYMBOLS / Change ↓' section header grows to about a quarter of the screen
The no-results search state uses a star icon instead of a magnifying glass
A.scroll: Smooth, native-feeling List scrolling with no blank rows or pop-in; live updates don't disturb the scroll, and the position is kept on returning from a detail screen. The section header is sticky and rows clip cleanly under it.

requirements.note: All 260 listed: star at leading edge, symbol/name stacked, price and coloured % text at trailing. Plain system list style.
Prices update every second in place, including during scrolls and flings; no flicker.

Sort is a system pull-down menu in the nav bar (Symbol/Price/Change + Descending Order toggle). The native bottom search bar filters by symbol or name, with a ContentUnavailableView-style 'No Matching Stocks' state.
Leading star toggles (filled black); the segmented control in the list switches All / My List; My List has an empty state; there is a star in the detail nav bar.
Detail is an inset-grouped list: name, big price, change, a 'Last 60 prices' line chart with low/high that grows live (29 samples after ~30 s), plus open and volume rows.
My List (RZC, TKTO), the selected segment and the sort (Price) all survived relaunch. The search text also persisted across relaunch, which is unusual and left a stale 'cedarzz' query showing.

bugs: The search query persists across relaunch, so the app can open to a filtered or empty list with a stale query
Once, accessibility reported the 'All' segment as selected while My List was visibly selected and shown
tells: The detail's headline price is drawn in grey (secondary colour), which looks disabled
The filled star is black/label colour rather than the yellow/orange tint you'd expect for a favourite
At the largest text size the row stars stay tiny and rows lay out inconsistently (some put the price beside the symbol, others stack it)
Section headers 'Price History' / 'Market Details' are a custom grey semibold style rather than standard list headers
Inline small title rather than a large title on the root screen
B.scroll: Feels exactly like a UIKit/SwiftUI list: content scrolls under the blurred nav bar and the floating glass search bar, flings decelerate naturally, live updates don't jump, and the position is kept after visiting a detail screen.

why: Both apps meet every requirement, including live updates while scrolling and persistence. B is built almost entirely from stock iOS parts (nav-bar sort menu, bottom glass search, system segmented control, inset-grouped detail, ContentUnavailable-style empty states) and is hard to tell from a hand-built app. A is more designed and arguably prettier (badges, a filled chart, a market-pulse card), but its cream background, custom pill segment and badge styling read as a custom theme rather than iOS. B's flaws (grey detail price, search text kept across relaunch) are smaller than A's platform departures.
